correctness.rationale: On the star with m leaves the Laplacian spectrum consists of 0, 1, and m+1, with explicitly displayed orthogonal projectors. These yield four entry types and two nontrivial diagonal numerators: \(Q_m(h)\) and \(P_m(h)\); off-diagonal entries are nonnegative by factored identities. The scalar Radau stability function has global minimum (5-3sqrt(3))/2, giving strict positivity for \(m\le10\). For \(m\ge11\), Q_m has two roots separated around 1, and P_m is positive up to h=3, negative at h=8, and positive for large h, while Descartes permits at most two positive roots. Hence exactly three nonnegative-time windows, including boundaries. Separate exact Fraction matrix/rational formula comparisons on 192 graph-timestep samples, plus 990 exact integer sign checks, passed. Finite checks supplement, rather than replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The exact claim concerns the full, non-convex set of positive Radau IIA endpoint timesteps on a fixed reversible unit star, including exactly three connected components if and only if the star has at least eleven leaves. Inspection of the relevant general positivity results, including Horváth (1998, 2005), shows universal method/problem-class step restrictions or positivity for restricted cones, not the all-initial-vector, star-specific three-interval classification. The Radau IIA numerical tests in Horváth (2005), Section 4.1, use a Dirichlet path heat discretization and selected initial vectors; they do not imply the star formulas, the twelve-vertex cutoff, or the later recovered positivity window. Nearby published numerical positivity records use distinct stability functions or graph families. Searches for alternate representations, parameters, and stronger coverage returned no equivalent claim. Potential unindexed specialized results remain a residual risk, not an assertion of absolute uniqueness.
residual_risks: Search-based novelty evidence is not a proof of uniqueness: other unindexed numerical-analysis papers, theses or tables could already contain these exact star-specific intervals.
The Numipedia method page itself was checked from an indexed table rather than full webpage text; its method formula was independently verified.
The current comparison does not assert exhaustion of all historical numerics sources; no independent audit was performed.

value.rationale: An L-stable third-order implicit integrator can preserve all positive initial states at arbitrarily large timestep on a fixed 12-vertex diffusion network yet fail at two separated intermediate timestep bands. The exact first graph-size threshold and full closed-form admissible set discriminate contractive spectral damping from positive-state preservation, and give an actionable timestep classification for benchmark network diffusion. The exact bound is neither a generic RK stability-region exercise nor an arbitrary parameter slice: unweighted stars are a natural minimally symmetric family exposing hub-versus-leaf obstructions.
